hints: Focus on the type of hydrolysis here, alkaline with NaOH is not the same as acid hydrolysis with dilute acid.
Split the ester ethyl propanoate at the C-O single bond, the carbonyl side becomes the carboxylate part and the O-alkyl side becomes the alcohol part.
Remember NaOH neutralises any carboxylic acid to its sodium salt, but ethanol is too weak an acid to react further with NaOH under these conditions.
walkthrough:
**Identify the ester**

Look carefully at the structure. The left side is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$ and the right side is $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. So this is ethyl propanoate.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall alkaline hydrolysis**

Heating an ester under reflux with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ causes base hydrolysis, also called saponification. It is irreversible because the base neutralises the acid product.

$$\text{ester + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{sodium carboxylate + alcohol}$$

**Form the two products**

The acyl part gives sodium propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$, not the free acid. The alkyl part gives ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, not sodium ethoxide.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Match to the table**

Product 1 must be the $\text{COONa}$ salt and product 2 must be the $\text{OH}$ alcohol. That combination matches only one row.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows propanoic acid plus ethanol. That would be the result of acid hydrolysis with dilute HCl or H2SO4. With excess NaOH, the acid cannot survive, it is immediately neutralised to the carboxylate salt.
options.B: Incorrect. This has both parts wrong way round. The carboxylic acid would not stay as COOH in base, and ethanol would not form ONa. Ethanol is a very weak acid and does not react with aqueous NaOH to give sodium ethoxide.
options.C: Correct. Well done. Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate gives sodium propanoate, CH3CH2COONa, as product 1 and ethanol, CH3CH2OH, as product 2. The base converts the acid fragment to its salt, while the alcohol fragment is unchanged.
options.D: Incorrect. The sodium propanoate part is right, but sodium ethoxide, CH3CH2ONa, is wrong. Sodium ethoxide is made from ethanol plus reactive sodium metal, not from ethanol plus aqueous NaOH. Under reflux with NaOH(aq), the alcohol stays as CH3CH2OH.
